examples.ko: 우리 팀은 겨울마다 제주도로 전지훈련을 가요.
examples.en: Our team goes to Jeju Island for a training camp every winter.

examples.ko: 야구 선수들이 따뜻한 곳에서 전지훈련을 해요.
examples.en: The baseball players do their camp training in a warm place.

examples.ko: 전지훈련 중에는 휴대폰을 마음대로 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: During the training camp, you can't use your phone freely.
This training camp takes place abroad for two weeks.

examples.ko: 전지훈련에서 돌아온 선수들이 많이 힘들어 보여요.
examples.en: The players back from the training camp look very tired.

examples.ko: 동생은 축구부 전지훈련에 참가하려고 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: My younger brother saved money to join the soccer club's training camp.

explain: 스포츠 팀이 평소 훈련하는 곳을 떠나 다른 지역이나 외국에서 하는 훈련이에요. '합숙 훈련'은 함께 지낸다는 점이, 전지훈련은 장소를 옮겨 간다는 점이 중심이에요. 보통 '전지훈련을 가다/떠나다/하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is training a sports team does away from its usual base, in another region or abroad. '합숙 훈련' focuses on living together, whereas 전지훈련 focuses on moving to another place. People usually say '전지훈련을 가다/떠나다/하다'.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 대충 읽지 말고 정독이 필요한 책이에요.
examples.en: This novel is a book that needs careful reading, not skimming.

examples.ko: 속독보다 정독이 이해에 더 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Close reading helps understanding more than speed reading.

examples.ko: 선생님은 방학 숙제로 소설 정독을 권하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher recommended reading a novel closely as vacation homework.

examples.ko: 정독 습관을 들이니까 글이 잘 이해돼요.
examples.en: Since I built a habit of close reading, I understand texts better.
I prefer close reading to reading many books.

examples.ko: 정독 후에 느낀 점을 짧게 써 오세요.
examples.en: Please write briefly about what you felt after reading it closely.

explain: 한 줄씩 뜻을 새기며 꼼꼼하게 읽는 방법을 말해요. 반대되는 말은 빨리 읽는 '속독', 책을 많이 읽는 '다독'이에요. 공부나 독서 이야기에서 '정독하다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to reading carefully, thinking about the meaning line by line. Its counterparts are '속독' (speed reading) and '다독' (reading many books). It often appears in talk about studying and reading, together with '정독하다'.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 교과서를 한 번 정독해요.
examples.en: I read the textbook closely once before the exam.
Be sure to read the contract closely before you sign.
I read the paper closely all night yesterday.

examples.ko: 이 책은 천천히 정독하면 훨씬 재미있어요.
examples.en: This book is much more fun if you read it slowly and carefully.
I started assembling after reading the manual carefully.

examples.ko: 한 줄씩 정독하려고 해도 자꾸 졸려요.
examples.en: Even when I try to read line by line, I keep getting sleepy.

explain: '읽다'보다 꼼꼼히 뜻을 따져 가며 읽는다는 느낌이 강해요. 책, 논문, 계약서, 설명서처럼 놓치면 안 되는 글에 잘 어울려요. 반대로 대충 빨리 읽을 때는 '속독하다', '훑어보다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '읽다', suggesting you read carefully and think through the meaning. It suits texts you must not misread, such as books, papers, contracts and manuals. For reading quickly, people say '속독하다' or '훑어보다'.

examples.ko: 친구들이 싸울 때마다 제가 중재자가 돼요.
examples.en: Whenever my friends fight, I become the mediator.

examples.ko: 두 회사 사이에서 중재자 역할을 맡았어요.
examples.en: I took the role of mediator between the two companies.

examples.ko: 중재자는 어느 한쪽 편을 들면 안 돼요.
examples.en: A mediator must not take either side.
I stepped in as a go-between for my parents and my older brother.

examples.ko: 노사 갈등을 풀려면 믿을 만한 중재자가 필요해요.
examples.en: To resolve the labor-management conflict, you need a trustworthy mediator.

examples.ko: 우리 반 반장은 늘 좋은 중재자예요.
examples.en: Our class president is always a good peacemaker.

explain: 싸움이나 갈등에서 양쪽 사이에 서서 풀어 주는 사람이에요. '중재자 역할을 하다/맡다', '중재에 나서다'처럼 많이 말해요. 법이나 계약 같은 공식적인 분쟁뿐 아니라 친구 사이 다툼에도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: This is the person who stands between two sides in a dispute and helps settle it. People say '중재자 역할을 하다/맡다' and '중재에 나서다'. It is used for formal disputes such as legal or contract matters, and also figuratively for quarrels between friends.

examples.en: A city is a collection of countless people and buildings.

examples.ko: 이 작품은 작은 조각들의 집합체로 보여요.
examples.en: This artwork looks like an assembly of small pieces.
Our body is exactly a collection of cells.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 스타 선수들의 집합체일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: That team is just a collection of star players.

examples.ko: 은하는 수많은 별이 모인 거대한 집합체라고 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned that a galaxy is a huge aggregation of countless stars.
It was a day that felt like a bundle of every possible problem.

explain: 보통 'A의 집합체'처럼 여러 개가 모여 하나가 된 덩어리를 말해요. 사람들이 모인 '모임'과 달리 물건, 세포, 요소 등에도 쓰고, '노력의 집합체'처럼 비유로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually used as 'A의 집합체', meaning a lump formed by many things gathered together. Unlike '모임' (a gathering of people), it also applies to objects, cells and elements, and figuratively as in '노력의 집합체'.

en: drafting; call-up; pulling someone for duty

examples.ko: 선수 차출 문제로 감독이 고민이 많아요.
examples.en: The coach is worried about the issue of releasing players.

examples.ko: 국가대표 차출 때문에 팀 경기에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: He missed the club match because he was called up to the national team.

examples.ko: 이번 행사에 직원 차출이 갑자기 결정됐어요.
examples.en: Pulling staff for this event was suddenly decided.
Many people oppose pulling manpower away.
I canceled my vacation because of a sudden assignment.
The team did not allow the players to be released.

explain: 어떤 일을 위해 사람을 원래 자리에서 빼 와 쓰는 것을 말해요. '선발'이 뽑아서 기회를 주는 느낌이라면, 차출은 하던 일에서 불려 간다는 느낌이 강해요. 국가대표 차출, 인력 차출처럼 스포츠와 회사 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: It means pulling people from their original place to use them for some task. While '선발' feels like choosing someone to give a chance, 차출 feels like being called away from what you were doing. It appears in sports (national team call-ups) and in workplace talk about manpower.

en: draft; call up; pull (someone) for duty

examples.ko: 회사에서 직원 세 명을 행사에 차출했어요.
examples.en: The company pulled three employees for the event.

examples.ko: 구단은 선수를 대표팀에 차출하지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The club decided not to release the player to the national team.

examples.ko: 급한 일이 생겨서 다른 부서 사람들을 차출해야 해요.
examples.en: Something urgent came up, so we have to pull people from other departments.

examples.ko: 대표팀이 선수들을 차출하면 시즌 경기가 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If the national team calls up the players, the season games get harder.

examples.ko: 시청에서 공무원을 차출해서 행사를 돕게 했어요.
examples.en: City Hall pulled civil servants to help with the event.
The coach said he would pull me for the team.

explain: 'A를 B에 차출하다'처럼 사람을 목적어로 써요. '뽑다'보다 원래 있던 자리에서 빼 와서 쓴다는 느낌이 강하고, 시키는 쪽의 결정이 중심이에요. 스포츠 기사나 회사 이야기에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It takes a person as the object, as in 'A를 B에 차출하다'. It feels more like pulling someone out of their original place than simply choosing them with '뽑다', and the decision lies with the one giving the order. You can see it in sports articles and workplace talk.

examples.en: We will begin the ceremony once all the guests are seated.
Passengers, please take your seats.

examples.ko: 면접관이 착석하라고 말할 때까지 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I stood until the interviewer told me to be seated.
Everyone is seated, so let's begin now.

examples.ko: 회의실에 착석한 사람은 아직 세 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: Only three people have taken their seats in the meeting room so far.

examples.ko: 비행기가 뜨기 전에 모두 착석하셔야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone must be seated before the plane takes off.

explain: '앉다'보다 격식을 차린 말이라서 안내 방송, 행사, 면접 같은 자리에서 자주 들려요. 친구와 대화할 때 쓰면 딱딱하게 들려서 보통은 '앉다'라고 해요. '착석해 주세요'처럼 부탁하는 표현으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '앉다', so you hear it in announcements, ceremonies and interviews. With friends it sounds stiff, so people usually just say '앉다'. A common pattern is the polite request '착석해 주세요'.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 총선거가 열려서 거리가 시끄러워요.
examples.en: A general election is being held next month, so the streets are noisy.
General election day is a public holiday, so we have the day off.

examples.ko: 이번 총선거에서 젊은 유권자의 투표율이 높았어요.
examples.en: Young voters' turnout was high in this general election.
I heard the general election results come out tonight.
I took part in a general election and voted for the first time.
Ahead of the general election, the candidates started campaigning.

explain: 국회의원을 한꺼번에 뽑는 선거를 말하고, 뉴스나 일상 대화에서는 보통 '총선'이라고 줄여요. 대통령을 뽑는 선거는 '대선'이라고 해서 구분해요. '총선거'는 공식적이고 격식 있는 말투예요.
explain_en: It refers to the election that chooses all members of the National Assembly at once, and in news and daily talk it is usually shortened to '총선'. The presidential election is called '대선', so the two are distinguished. '총선거' sounds more official and formal.

examples.en: I played games all night, so my eyes are bloodshot.
My eyes turned red and bloodshot, so I went to the hospital.
Your eyes are bloodshot, maybe from crying.

examples.ko: 렌즈를 오래 끼면 눈이 충혈되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you wear contact lenses for a long time, your eyes easily get bloodshot.
Everyone was worried when I came to work with bloodshot eyes.
I put in eye drops so my eyes wouldn't get bloodshot.

explain: '눈이 충혈되다'처럼 대부분 눈에 대해 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '눈이 빨개지다', '눈에 핏발이 서다'라고도 해요. 피곤하거나 울었거나 눈에 병이 났을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Most often it is used for eyes, as in '눈이 충혈되다'. In daily talk people also say '눈이 빨개지다' or '눈에 핏발이 서다'. It describes eyes after tiredness, crying or an eye infection.

examples.en: When the power went out, the room became pitch dark.

examples.ko: 칠흑 같은 밤길을 혼자 걸으니 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Walking alone on the pitch-dark night road was scary.

examples.ko: 할머니는 젊을 때 칠흑 같은 머리카락이 아름다웠대요.
examples.en: They say my grandmother's jet-black hair was beautiful when she was young.

examples.ko: 산속은 칠흑 같은 어둠에 싸여 있었어요.
examples.en: The mountains were wrapped in pitch-black darkness.
There was no moon, so the sky was jet-black.

examples.ko: 칠흑 속에서 작은 불빛이 하나 보였어요.
examples.en: A small light appeared in the pitch darkness.

explain: 거의 '칠흑 같은 어둠/밤', '칠흑같이 어둡다'처럼 굳은 짝으로 써요. 머리카락이나 눈동자가 아주 까만 것도 비유로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '깜깜하다', '캄캄하다'가 더 가벼운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in fixed pairings such as '칠흑 같은 어둠/밤' and '칠흑같이 어둡다'. It can also describe very black hair or eyes figuratively. In everyday talk, '깜깜하다' and '캄캄하다' are the lighter words.

examples.en: This movie is a modern version of the story of Sim Cheong.
These days the internet is a modern-day library.
A modern Cinderella story came out as a drama.
His friends call him a modern-day Hong Gildong.
They remade the old tale as a modern version.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 현대판 장터 같은 분위기예요.
examples.en: This shop has the feel of a modern-day market.

explain: '현대판 + 명사'나 '~의 현대판'처럼 쓰고, 옛이야기·인물·제도를 오늘날에 맞게 바꾼 것을 말해요. '현대판 홍길동'처럼 비유로 많이 써요. 원래 이야기는 '원작'이나 '고전'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is used as '현대판 + noun' or '~의 현대판' for an old story, figure or system adapted to today. It is often figurative, as in '현대판 홍길동'. The original is called '원작' or '고전'.

examples.ko: 어제 우리 팀 선발투수가 호투를 펼쳤어요.
examples.en: Our team's starting pitcher pitched very well yesterday.
Thanks to the great pitching, the team won 3 to 1.

examples.ko: 신인 투수의 호투가 팬들을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: The rookie pitcher's strong performance surprised the fans.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 시즌 초반 호투로 주목받았어요.
examples.en: That player drew attention with his good pitching early in the season.
Despite the great pitching, the team ended up losing.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기의 호투 장면을 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the great pitching moments from today's game again.

explain: 야구에서 투수가 잘 던지는 것을 말하고, 기사 제목에도 자주 나와요. '호투를 펼치다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 반대로 못 던질 때는 '부진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes a pitcher throwing well in baseball and often appears in article headlines. '호투를 펼치다' is a common pairing. When a pitcher does poorly, people say '부진'.

examples.en: The starting pitcher pitched well through the seventh inning.

examples.ko: 그 투수가 계속 호투하면 우승할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If that pitcher keeps pitching well, we can win the title.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 호투하고도 승리를 못 얻었어요.
examples.en: He pitched well in yesterday's game but didn't get the win.

examples.ko: 신인 선수가 강팀을 상대로 호투해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The rookie pitched well against a strong team and became a talking point.
I'll look forward to him pitching well today too.

examples.ko: 부상 후 첫 경기에서 호투한 모습에 팬들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Fans applauded him for pitching well in his first game after the injury.

explain: 주어는 거의 투수이고, 야구 중계나 기사에서 많이 들려요. 일상 대화에서 '잘 던지다'라고 말하는 것을 조금 격식 있게 쓴 말이에요. 팀이 이겼는지와 상관없이 투수가 잘 던졌을 때 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: The subject is almost always a pitcher, and you hear it in baseball broadcasts and articles. It is a slightly more formal version of '잘 던지다' in daily talk. You can use it whenever the pitcher threw well, whether or not the team won.

examples.en: The teacher called the students with a loudspeaker.
The candidate greeted people holding a megaphone.
The playground is big, so we need a loudspeaker.

examples.ko: 확성기 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The loudspeaker was so loud that I was startled.

examples.ko: 저 확성기는 고장이 났는지 소리가 끊겨요.
examples.en: That loudspeaker seems broken because the sound keeps cutting out.

examples.ko: 축제 때 확성기에서 신나는 음악이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Upbeat music came out of the loudspeaker during the festival.

explain: 소리를 크게 키워서 멀리까지 들리게 하는 장치예요. 학교 운동장, 선거 유세, 축제처럼 넓은 곳에서 쓰고, 손에 들고 쓰는 것은 '메가폰'이라고도 해요. '스피커'는 컴퓨터나 오디오에서 소리가 나오는 장치를 가리키는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is a device that makes sound louder so it carries far. It is used in wide places such as school playgrounds, election campaigns and festivals, and the hand-held kind is also called a '메가폰'. '스피커' more often refers to the part of a computer or audio system that outputs sound.

examples.en: There is a famous orchestra in our city.

examples.ko: 관현악단 연주회 표를 두 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two tickets for the orchestra concert.

examples.ko: 그 관현악단은 매년 해외 공연을 가요.
examples.en: That orchestra goes on overseas tours every year.
My younger sibling plays the violin in the school orchestra.
The orchestra and the choir went on stage together.
The conductor entered leading the orchestra.

explain: 현악기, 관악기, 타악기가 함께 연주하는 단체를 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '오케스트라'라고 많이 하고, '관현악단'은 공연 안내나 뉴스 같은 격식 있는 글에서 볼 수 있어요. '교향악단'도 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It means a group in which string, wind and percussion instruments play together. In daily talk people often say '오케스트라', while '관현악단' appears in concert notices and news, which are more formal. '교향악단' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: The news of the defection was covered widely.

examples.ko: 그는 귀순 후 새 삶을 시작했어요.
examples.en: After defecting, he started a new life.
There are organizations that help defectors.
This defection happened by sea.
They say there were many difficulties during the defection.
I'm curious about why he decided to defect.

explain: 뉴스에서 주로 남북 관계 이야기에 나오고, '귀순자'처럼도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '넘어오다'라고 하기도 해요. '귀순 의사를 밝히다'처럼 격식 있는 문장에 어울려요.
explain_en: It mainly appears in news about relations between South and North Korea and is also used as '귀순자'. In daily talk people may say '넘어오다'. It fits formal sentences such as '귀순 의사를 밝히다'.

examples.en: That soldier defected at dawn.
People who want to defect cross over at great risk.

examples.ko: 그가 귀순하고 나서 한국 생활에 적응했어요.
examples.en: After he defected, he adapted to life in Korea.
People who have defected receive settlement education.
He made up his mind to defect together with his family.

examples.ko: 몇 년 전에 귀순해서 지금은 회사에 다녀요.
examples.en: He defected a few years ago and now works at a company.

explain: 주어는 사람이고 '남한으로 귀순하다'처럼 어디로 오는지 같이 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 주로 보이는 격식 있는 말이에요. 같은 뜻을 일상에서는 '넘어오다'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The subject is a person, and it is used with the destination, as in '남한으로 귀순하다'. It is a formal word seen mostly in news and articles. In daily speech people may express the same idea as '넘어오다'.

examples.en: The score difference between the two teams is slim.
I missed first place by a narrow margin.
Our candidate is leading by a slim margin.

examples.ko: 두 제품은 가격 차이가 근소해서 고르기 어려워요.
examples.en: The price difference between the two products is tiny, so it's hard to choose.

examples.ko: 표 차이는 근소했지만 결과는 바뀌지 않았어요.
examples.en: The vote gap was slim, but the result didn't change.
I thought it would be close, but the gap was big.

explain: 점수, 표, 가격처럼 수나 양의 차이가 아주 작을 때 써요. '근소한 차이로 이기다/지다', '근소하게 앞서다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 사람이나 기분에는 쓰지 않고, 반대로 차이가 클 때는 '크다'나 '현저하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a difference in numbers or amounts, such as scores, votes or prices, is very small. '근소한 차이로 이기다/지다' and '근소하게 앞서다' are common pairings. It is not used for people or feelings, and for a big difference people say '크다' or '현저하다'.

examples.en: An anonymous donor gave a scholarship fund.

examples.ko: 할머니는 평생 모은 돈을 학교에 기탁하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother donated the money she saved all her life to the school.
The company decided to donate funds to help neighbors in need.
I'm sorting my books to donate them to the library.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 매년 쌀을 복지관에 기탁해요.
examples.en: This shop donates rice to the welfare center every year.
The donated funds are used for neighbors in need.

explain: 일상에서는 '기부하다'를 더 많이 말하고, 기탁하다는 성금, 장학금, 물품을 어떤 기관이나 단체에 맡겨 쓰게 할 때 뉴스 기사에서 볼 수 있어요. 'A가 B에 C를 기탁하다'처럼 받는 곳을 '~에'로 써요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '기부하다' more, while 기탁하다 appears in news articles when funds, scholarships or goods are entrusted to an organization to be used. The recipient is marked with '~에', as in 'A가 B에 C를 기탁하다'.

examples.en: The ball the batter hit became a grounder.
The shortstop caught the ground ball and threw it to first base.
The runner advanced to third on an infield grounder.
It was a pity that he grounded out.
That pitcher is good at inducing ground balls.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 땅볼보다 뜬공을 많이 쳐요.
examples.en: That player hits more fly balls than ground balls.

explain: 야구에서 땅 위로 구르는 공을 말해요. 반대로 공중으로 뜨는 공은 '뜬공'이라고 해요. '땅볼 아웃', '내야 땅볼'처럼 중계나 기사에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is a baseball term for a ball that rolls along the ground. The opposite, a ball hit into the air, is a '뜬공'. You often hear it as '땅볼 아웃' or '내야 땅볼' in broadcasts and articles.

examples.en: I played all night, but my mind is still clear.

examples.ko: 넘어졌는데 다친 데 없이 몸이 말짱했어요.
examples.en: I fell down, but my body was fine without any injury.

examples.ko: 세탁했는데도 옷이 말짱한 걸 보니 소재가 좋은가 봐요.
examples.en: The clothes look fine even after washing, so the fabric must be good.
The computer that was working fine suddenly shut off.
You said you were sick, but your face looks perfectly fine.

examples.ko: 겉은 말짱해 보여도 속은 다 상했어요.
examples.en: It looks intact on the outside, but it's all spoiled inside.

explain: '멀쩡하다'와 비슷하게 다치거나 망가진 데 없이 온전할 때 써요. '정신이 말짱하다'처럼 졸리거나 흐릿하지 않고 또렷하다는 뜻으로도 많이 말해요. 사람의 몸, 물건, 정신 상태에 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Like '멀쩡하다', it is used when something or someone is intact, without injury or damage. It is also commonly used for a clear mind, as in '정신이 말짱하다', meaning not sleepy or hazy. It works for a person's body, objects and mental state.

examples.en: They are investigating the cause of the accident thoroughly.

examples.ko: 계약 내용을 면밀히 살펴본 뒤에 서명했어요.
examples.en: I signed after examining the contract carefully.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 검사 결과를 면밀히 확인했어요.
examples.en: The doctor checked the test results closely.
If you look into it closely, there are problems.

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 글을 면밀히 읽고 의견을 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher read my writing closely and gave me feedback.
I'll decide after watching the situation closely.

explain: '꼼꼼히'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있는 말이에요. 조사하다, 검토하다, 분석하다, 살피다, 지켜보다 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. 방을 정리하는 것 같은 가벼운 일에는 '꼼꼼히'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '꼼꼼히' but more formal, and goes well with verbs such as 조사하다, 검토하다, 분석하다, 살피다 and 지켜보다. For light tasks like tidying a room, '꼼꼼히' sounds more natural.

en: truly deserving of the name; genuine

examples.en: He is truly the best singer in our country, in name and reality.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 명실상부하게 문화의 중심이 되었어요.
examples.en: This city has become the cultural center in both name and reality.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 명실상부 우리나라 최고의 대학이에요.
examples.en: This school is truly the best university in our country, in name and in fact.

examples.ko: 그가 명실상부하다는 평가를 받는 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a reason he is regarded as truly deserving of the title.

examples.ko: 명실상부하려면 이름뿐 아니라 실력도 있어야 해요.
examples.en: To live up to the name, you need real skill, not just the name.

examples.ko: 작은 가게였는데 이제는 명실상부한 맛집이 됐어요.
examples.en: It was a small shop, but now it's a truly famous restaurant.

explain: 소문이나 이름과 실제가 서로 맞을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. 주로 '명실상부한 + 명사'(최고, 1위, 강팀)로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '이름값을 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a compliment used when reputation or title and reality match. It is mostly used as '명실상부한 + noun', such as 최고, 1위 or 강팀. In daily talk people also say '이름값을 하다'.

examples.en: The police released a composite sketch of the suspect.
I heard the sketch looks a lot like the real face.
It took a long time to make the composite sketch.

examples.ko: 영화에서 짧은 장면을 이어 붙이는 몽타주 기법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned the montage technique of joining short scenes in film.
The composite picture was distributed nationwide.

examples.ko: 이 뮤직비디오는 여러 장면을 몽타주로 엮었어요.
examples.en: This music video weaves many scenes together as a montage.

explain: 영화에서 짧은 장면을 이어 붙이는 편집 기법을 말해요. 한국어에서는 목격자의 설명으로 만든 용의자 얼굴 그림이나 사진도 '몽타주'라고 하는데, 영어로는 보통 'composite sketch'라고 해요. 뉴스에서 '몽타주를 공개하다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the film-editing technique of joining short scenes. In Korean, 몽타주 also means a suspect's face drawn or pieced together from a witness's description, which English usually calls a 'composite sketch'. In news it often appears as '몽타주를 공개하다'.
